common_mistakes: Assuming the default scaling is orthonormal.
Inverting with a different norm than the forward call.
Asking fft for a one-sided power spectrum.
conventions: A real array is a list of numbers.
Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
At most 4096 elements are accepted. One complex number counts as one element.
The default norm is backward, not ortho. An inverse call must use the same norm.
Bins follow SciPy's fft order: the zero frequency is first.
tools.name: fft
tools.one_sentence: Compute a one-dimensional discrete Fourier transform.

parameters.description: The 1-D sequence. A real array is a list of numbers. Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
parameters.name: x

parameters.description: Scaling. backward is NumPy's usual unnormalized forward transform.
parameters.name: norm

tools.purpose: Transform a 1-D sequence into frequency bins, or restore the sequence.
related: power_spectrum returns frequencies in hertz and one-sided power for a real signal.
convolve is linear convolution, not multiplication of Fourier transforms.
tools.returns: A complex sequence of the same length, with shape, dtype, re, and im. The inverse of a forward transform uses the same norm and restores the input.
tools.when_not: You want the one-sided power of a real recording. Use power_spectrum.
tools.when_to_use: You need the forward or inverse discrete Fourier transform of one sequence.

common_mistakes: Treating power as a density in units of power per hertz.
Ignoring frequencies_hz and assuming a bin index is already in hertz.
conventions: Input is real. A complex object is rejected.
At most 4096 elements are accepted. One complex number counts as one element.
frequencies_hz[0] is 0 Hz. The last bin is the Nyquist frequency when n is even.
power is abs(rfft(samples))^2 divided by the number of samples.
tools.name: power_spectrum
tools.one_sentence: Compute the one-sided power spectrum of a real signal.

parameters.description: Sample rate in hertz. Must be positive.
parameters.name: sample_rate_hz

tools.purpose: Report frequency bins in hertz and the one-sided power of a real sequence.
related: fft is the transform to use when you will invert it or the input is complex.
tools.returns: frequencies_hz from rfftfreq, power equal to abs(rfft)^2 / n, plus shape and dtype. This is not a power spectral density.
tools.when_not: The series is complex, or you need a transform you can invert. Use fft.
tools.when_to_use: You have real samples and a sample rate, and you want power per frequency.

common_mistakes: Using valid when the requested length is the length of a. That is same.
Expecting the edges to wrap. This is linear convolution.
conventions: A real array is a list of numbers.
Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
At most 4096 elements are accepted. One complex number counts as one element.
full returns every overlap, including partial ones at the ends.
same returns the central part and has the same length as a.
valid returns only positions where b lies entirely inside a.
tools.name: convolve

parameters.description: The first 1-D sequence. A real array is a list of numbers. Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
parameters.name: a

parameters.description: The second 1-D sequence. A real array is a list of numbers. Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
parameters.name: b

parameters.description: Which part of the full convolution to keep.
parameters.name: mode

tools.purpose: Compute the linear convolution of two 1-D sequences.
related: fft does not replace this tool. This tool is linear convolution.
tools.returns: The convolved sequence, with shape, dtype, and either values or re and im. same has the length of a. valid keeps only complete overlaps.
tools.when_not: You want circular convolution. This tool does not wrap the edges.
tools.when_to_use: You want linear convolution in full, same, or valid mode.

common_mistakes: Passing a rectangular matrix. The error tells you to use least_squares.
Ignoring a singular error and treating a failure as a numeric answer.
conventions: A real array is a list of numbers.
Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
At most 4096 elements are accepted. One complex number counts as one element.
A must have the same number of rows and columns.
b has one entry per row.
residual_norm near zero means the solution fits A x = b.
tools.name: solve_linear_system

parameters.description: The matrix A. It must be square. A real array is a list of numbers. Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
parameters.name: a

parameters.description: The right-hand side, one value per row of A.
parameters.name: b

tools.purpose: Solve A x = b when A is square.
related: least_squares minimizes ||A x - b|| when A is not square or not invertible.
tools.returns: The solution vector, with shape, dtype, and residual_norm, the 2-norm of A x - b.
tools.when_not: A is rectangular or singular. Use least_squares.
tools.when_to_use: A is square and you want the direct solution plus a residual.

common_mistakes: Reading residual_norm as zero when the system is only approximately consistent.
Ignoring rank when several solutions fit equally well.
conventions: A real array is a list of numbers.
Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
At most 4096 elements are accepted. One complex number counts as one element.
b has one entry per row of A, not per column.
rank below the number of columns means the solution is not unique.
tools.name: least_squares

parameters.description: The matrix A, square or rectangular. A real array is a list of numbers. Complex values are {"re": [...], "im": [...]} with matching shapes.
parameters.name: a

parameters.description: The right-hand side, one value per row of A.
parameters.name: b

tools.purpose: Find x that minimizes the 2-norm of A x - b.
related: solve_linear_system is the direct solver for a square invertible matrix.
tools.returns: The solution vector, residual_norm (the 2-norm of A x - b), and rank.
tools.when_not: A is square and invertible. Use solve_linear_system for that case.
tools.when_to_use: A is rectangular, or a square system may be singular.
